name: DNDReader 0.3.0 — Ubuntu, Windows and Android
body:
Select text in a PDF, tap **Find meaning**, and Google results open in a panel inside the reader. Close it and your scroll position is exactly where you left it.

No AI, no API keys, no backend, no account, no telemetry.

**The first published release, and the first to cover three platforms with one version number.**

## New: Android

- Touch text selection with drag handles and a magnifier
- A draggable bottom-sheet search panel on the **system WebView** — nothing like Chromium is bundled, so the APK is ~25 MB against the desktop bundle's ~326 MB
- Open PDFs from the Android picker or by sharing to the app (`VIEW` / `SEND` intents)
- Layered system back, edge-to-edge, state restored after the OS kills the app
- `INTERNET` is the only permission — no storage permissions at all

## Ubuntu and Windows

Unchanged in behaviour. The Android work touched no file under `linux/`, `windows/` or `packaging/`. Both are rebuilt from this tag, so the binaries are new even though the behaviour is not.

Verified against the real browser engines: **Linux 10/10, Windows 11/11, Android 11/11** conformance.

## Install

**Ubuntu** (26.04; `Depends` are derived from the build machine's libraries)
```bash
sudo apt install ./dndreader_0.3.0-1_amd64.deb
```

**Windows 10 1809+** — run `DNDReader-0.3.0-setup-x64.exe`. Unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn.

**Android 8.0+** — take `DNDReader-0.3.0-arm64-v8a.apk` for any phone from roughly 2017 on. Use `armeabi-v7a` only for older 32-bit devices, `x86_64` only for emulators. You will need to allow installing from unknown sources.

All APKs are signed with the release key, certificate SHA-256:
```
90:B1:F8:9D:69:CA:9F:26:14:0A:AC:C9:DC:B2:A8:A5:BF:49:43:97:F1:BF:E1:99:A1:26:02:7F:A7:17:D9:36
```

## Known limitations

- **Android holds a private copy of each document.** Edits to the original will not appear until you open or share it again.
- **Memory on Android is higher than budgeted** — about 517 MB with a 240-page document open and the search panel alive, against a 300 MB target. Fine on the test device; reported rather than quietly re-baselined.
- You cannot sign in to Google in the panel — Google blocks sign-in in embedded webviews. Results are signed-out.
- Text-based PDFs only. No OCR.
- Not verified: TalkBack, Bluetooth keyboard/mouse/stylus, split screen, Android 13+ on physical hardware, a missing or very old system WebView. See `docs/android-owner-test.md`.
- Whether Google's terms permit loading Search inside a third-party app panel is **not established** — see `docs/implementation-plan.md` §9.8.
